data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"There are 648 valid three-digit numbers with all distinct digits, determined by the chromatic polynomial of a complete graph K_3 equipped with a vertex-restricted color list.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The claim is falsified if the palette is not uniformly available to the unrestricted positions.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The claim fails if the constraint 'all three digits different' is interpreted as a path graph P_3 rather than a complete graph K_3 (though for 3 vertices, path coloring allows the ends to match, which violates the problem's criteria).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The problem of assigning distinct digits to positions (H, T, U) maps to a proper vertex coloring of a complete graph K_3. An edge connects every pair of positions, enforcing inequality. The digits 0-9 form the color palette. The H vertex has a list of 9 colors (1-9), while T and U have lists of 10 colors (0-9). Evaluating the chromatic polynomial for K_3 under these list constraints yields the product of available choices: 9 for H, 9 for T, and 8 for U, totaling 648.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
